parameters.name: Symmetric AEAD
parameters.value: AES-256-GCM, 256-bit keys, 96-bit IV, 128-bit tag
parameters.notes: IV from a CSPRNG, generated inside packages/crypto; AAD is a canonical context (CP-15). ADR-003

parameters.name: Asymmetric key wrapping
parameters.value: RSA-OAEP, 3072-bit modulus, e = 65537, SHA-256 for OAEP and MGF1, OAEP label = canonical context
parameters.notes: Proposed, ADR-007. Maximum message 318 bytes. Used only on 32-byte random values: room key material, SEKs and the vault pair-check value. Never used on content (INV-17)

parameters.name: Key derivation for key separation
parameters.value: HKDF-SHA-256 (RFC 5869), salt = 32 zero bytes, info = canonical context, output 256 bits
parameters.notes: Inputs are uniformly random (RKM) or Argon2id output (VRK)

parameters.name: Vault KDF (browser)
parameters.value: Argon2id v1.3 (RFC 9106), 128-bit random salt per vault write, 256-bit output used only as HKDF input keying material. Target (every new vault and upgrade): m = 65536 KiB, t = 3, p = 1. Floor (lowest accepted): m = 19456 KiB, t = 2, p = 1. Ceiling (highest accepted): m = 262144 KiB, t = 10, p = 4
parameters.notes: Final, Phase 4 (benchmark in section 8). At the target one derivation in a fresh Web Worker took a median 263 ms in Chromium, 299 ms in Firefox and 321 ms in WebKit on the development laptop. No phone was measured (L-37); mid-range phones are expected to be several times slower, which is why the target was not raised to fill the 0.5 to 1.5 s band on the laptop. The ceiling bounds the work a modified record can make a browser do. The browser and the API both refuse records outside floor and ceiling. A vault below the target is offered an upgrade after unlock (ADR-010). ADR-010

parameters.name: Server password hashing
parameters.value: Argon2id v1.3 (RFC 9106), 128-bit random salt, 256-bit output, PHC string. Final (Phase 3): m = 65536 KiB, t = 3, p = 4 (the target, RFC 9106 second recommended option). Floor for accepting stored hashes: m = 19456 KiB, t = 2, p = 1
parameters.notes: Adopted after the Phase 3 benchmark (section 7): 294 ms median on a 2-vCPU, 2 GiB container at the API's concurrency limit of 2, under the 500 ms rule. Hashes with other parameters are rehashed at the next successful login. The API runs at most min(4, CPUs) computations at once with 32 queued; beyond that it answers 503 (T-26). Re-run pnpm bench:argon2 on the production VM in Phase 17 and record it here

parameters.name: Secret input policy
parameters.value: Auth password 12 to 128 characters. Vault Passphrase 16 to 256 characters. Both checked against a local blocklist; no composition rules; Unicode NFKC normalization before hashing or derivation
parameters.notes: Normalization keeps derivation identical across devices and input methods. Auth password implemented in Phase 3: lengths in Unicode code points after NFKC, never truncated; lone surrogates refused; local blocklist of 30,402 breached passwords of 12 or more characters (UK NCSC top 100,000 and the Pwdb top one million, SecLists, pinned and checksum-verified, built by scripts/auth/build-password-blocklist.mjs); passwords containing the email local part, display name or product name refused. Nothing is sent to a third party. Vault Passphrase implemented in Phase 4 (packages/crypto/src/passphrase.ts): the same length rules with 16 to 256 code points, whitespace kept as typed; a local blocklist of 3,350 entries of 16 or more characters from the same pinned sources; the same identity checks. It runs only in the browser, at setup and change, never at unlock, because the passphrase never reaches the server

parameters.name: Hash function
parameters.notes: Fingerprints, ciphertext hashes, audit chain, digests of high-entropy tokens. Never for passwords

parameters.name: Sessions
parameters.value: 256-bit random token, base64url, stored as SHA-256 digest. Idle timeout 30 minutes, absolute lifetime 12 hours, at most 10 active sessions per user, pre-authentication (MFA pending) state 5 minutes
parameters.notes: Rotation and invalidation events in session-and-csrf.md. ADR-008

parameters.name: TOTP
parameters.value: RFC 6238, HMAC-SHA-1, 6 digits, 30-second step, accept plus or minus 1 step, 160-bit secret, replay protection by last used step
parameters.notes: SHA-1 is kept for authenticator-app compatibility. HMAC-SHA-1 does not depend on SHA-1 collision resistance

parameters.name: Recovery codes
parameters.value: 10 codes, each at least 100 bits of entropy, stored as SHA-256 digests, single use
parameters.notes: High-entropy random values may use a fast hash; passwords may not

parameters.name: Server-side encryption of TOTP secrets
parameters.value: AES-256-GCM under TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY (32 bytes, secret file), random 96-bit IV, AAD = canonical context with user ID, key ID stored for rotation
parameters.notes: The only server-decryptable user secret. Implemented in Phase 3: stored as IV, ciphertext and tag (48 bytes for a 160-bit secret); AAD is the context cm.srv.totp with keyId and userId; any mismatch fails closed. One active key; rotating it needs a re-encryption tool that does not exist yet (L-31)

parameters.name: Login identifier HMAC
parameters.value: HMAC-SHA-256 under IDENTIFIER_HMAC_KEY over the NFKC-normalized, lower-cased identifier
parameters.notes: Lets rate limiting correlate unknown identifiers without storing them

parameters.name: Audit hash chain
parameters.value: eventHash = SHA-256(ASCII "CM-AUDIT-v1", byte 0x00, JCS(record)). The record contains seq and prevHash; prevHash of seq 1 is 64 hex zeros
parameters.notes: ADR-009

parameters.name: Audit checkpoint signature
parameters.value: Level 1 (baseline): Ed25519 (RFC 8032) via Node.js crypto, private key in a secret file mounted only into the worker container, public keys and revoked key IDs committed to the repository. Level 2 (optional): provider-managed non-exportable signing key (OCD-13). Checkpoints hourly, after security-critical events and on demand; external witness copy at least weekly
parameters.notes: Trust model in ADR-009 section 8. Optional RFC 3161 timestamp token (OCD-08)

parameters.name: Canonical encoding
parameters.value: RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme. Allowed values: strings, safe integers, booleans, null, objects, arrays. No floating-point numbers. Timestamps as ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds. 64-bit integers as decimal strings. Binary as unpadded base64url strings
parameters.notes: Used for AAD, OAEP labels, HKDF info, signed statements and audit records. Phase 4: implemented in the repository for this subset (LIB-05); context objects are built only by packages/crypto/src/contexts.ts, which fixes the field set of every context and validates each field

parameters.name: Key usage bounds
parameters.value: A DEK encrypts at most 2 messages (file content and manifest; a NEK or SEK encrypts one). RWK_v wraps at most 2^20 DEKs (server-enforced wrapCount, then rotation). Each private-key wrapping key (one per private key, CP-27) wraps exactly one key per vault write; every write uses a fresh salt and therefore new wrapping keys
parameters.notes: NIST SP 800-38D limits random-IV GCM to 2^32 invocations per key. CipherMesh stays far below

parameters.name: Identity fingerprint
parameters.value: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 serialization of the context cm.identity.fingerprint {suite, encryptionKeySpki, signingKeySpki} (both DER SPKI encodings as base64url), displayed as 64 hex characters in 16 groups of 4, always compared in full
parameters.notes: Revised by ADR-015 before any identity existed. One comparison covers both public keys. Each client computes the fingerprint from the keys it actually uses and never displays a server-supplied value as verified

parameters.name: Algorithm suite CM1
parameters.notes: Stored on every encrypted record. CP-26 joined the suite through ADR-015 before any CM1 record existed

parameters.name: Maximum file size (single-shot encryption)
parameters.value: 50 MiB in the baseline
parameters.notes: Raising it requires a browser memory benchmark. Much larger files need the chunked design in OCD-09. Phase 7 benchmark (section 9): pnpm bench:files encrypts and decrypts 50 MiB in about 150 ms (Chromium, Firefox) to 0.9 s (WebKit) with a byte-exact round trip on the development laptop. Memory was bounded by analysis, not measured (no engine reported page memory), and no phone was tested, so the 50 MiB baseline stays and L-47 records the gap; the limit is enforced in packages/crypto (FILES.maxPlaintextBytes), in the request schema, by a database CHECK and by the signed content length of the upload URL

parameters.name: Presigned URL lifetime
parameters.value: Upload (PUT) at most 5 minutes, download (GET) at most 60 seconds
parameters.notes: Implemented in Phase 7 (apps/api/src/storage/object-store.ts): AWS Signature Version 4 query authentication; the upload URL signs the exact content length; the download URL forces attachment and application/octet-stream; expiry and size binding are tested against the local emulator (EV-07-06)

parameters.name: TLS
parameters.value: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 only, Mozilla "intermediate" configuration (ECDHE with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305), ECDSA P-256 certificates from Let's Encrypt; HSTS staged: 0, then 86400 seconds for the demonstration once HTTPS and renewal are verified, one year in a longer-lived deployment; no includeSubDomains or preload
parameters.notes: The database hop uses TLS 1.3 only with sslmode=verify-full against the deployment's private CA (CD-34, ADR-014)

parameters.name: Vault auto-lock
parameters.value: 15 minutes without user activity, and on logout, tab close or session invalidation
parameters.notes: Client-side behaviour; cannot be enforced by the server

parameters.name: Randomness
parameters.value: Browser: crypto.getRandomValues and WebCrypto generateKey. Server: crypto.randomBytes, crypto.randomUUID
parameters.notes: Math.random forbidden

parameters.name: Room Safety Code
parameters.value: RSC_v = HKDF-SHA-256(IKM = RKM_v, salt = 32 zero bytes, info = context cm.room.safety-code with roomId and keyVersion, 32 bytes). Display the first 66 bits as six 11-bit indices into a fixed 2048-word list (LIB-08), with the key version; numeric alternative: the same 66 bits as 20 decimal digits
parameters.notes: Computed only in the browser, never sent or stored (INV-18). ADR-012. Implemented in Phase 6 (packages/crypto/src/room-keys.ts, computeSafetyCode): indices most significant first, digits zero-padded to 20. Known-answer vector for RKM = 00 01 .. 1f, room 0f3e2d1c-4b5a-4968-8776-a5b4c3d2e1f0, version 1: "knee want dad also trust siege", 35631199793402506816; reproduced by OpenSSL in Node.js and in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit

parameters.name: Rekey operations
parameters.value: Lease 10 minutes; at most one PENDING operation per room; at most 10 operation starts per room per hour; at most 100 members plus pending invitees per room, which bounds a finalize request to 100 envelopes
parameters.notes: ADR-013

parameters.name: Identity signing key
parameters.value: ECDSA on P-256 with SHA-256 (FIPS 186-5), signatures in IEEE P1363 form (r and s, 64 bytes), public key as a 91-byte DER SPKI with an uncompressed point
parameters.notes: Phase 4, ADR-015. Signs only canonical statements: cm.identity.binding, cm.vault.rewrap, and the room statements of Phase 6. Never encrypts or wraps. Nonces come from WebCrypto or Node.js, never from CipherMesh code. Imported public keys must re-export byte for byte

parameters.name: Vault format, version 1
parameters.value: VRK = Argon2id(NFKC passphrase, salt, CP-04), imported at once as a non-extractable HKDF key. One wrapping key per private key: HKDF(VRK, info = cm.vault.pk-wrap {userId, keyId, purpose}). Each private key is wrapped as PKCS#8 with AES-256-GCM, AAD = cm.vault.private-key {userId, keyId, purpose, fingerprint, suite, vaultVersion}. Unlock imports both keys as non-extractable and runs pair checks
parameters.notes: Phase 4. Records with another version or suite are refused (no downgrade). Wrapped sizes: encryption key 1,700 to 2,048 bytes, signing key 64 to 256 bytes. Specification: vault.md

parameters.name: Note size and revisions (Phase 8)
parameters.value: Note document (RFC 8785 {body, title, v}) at most 64 KiB (65,536 bytes), so its ciphertext is at most 65,552 bytes; title 1 to 200 UTF-16 code units without control or bidirectional-override characters; revisions 1 to 2^31 - 1; at most 1000 live notes per room
parameters.notes: Decision D-08-01 (phase-08-traceability.md). No earlier document fixed a note size. 64 KiB keeps the largest request (ciphertext as base64url plus the other fields, about 88 KiB) inside the API's 128 KiB body limit, which stays unchanged, and is one AES-GCM message in every browser. Enforced in packages/crypto (NOTES), the request schemas, a database CHECK and packages/shared (NOTE_LIMITS); a test compares all of them with this row

parameters.name: Secret size, lifetime and limits (Phase 9)
parameters.value: Secret document (RFC 8785 {text, v}) at most 16 KiB (16,384 bytes), so its payload ciphertext is 17 to 16,400 bytes; the text is at least one character of well-formed Unicode; lifetime at least 5 minutes and at most the PC-09 maximum of the room's profile (7 days, 72 hours, 24 hours); at most 100 ACTIVE, unexpired secrets sent per account; the wrapped SEK is one RSA-OAEP-3072 block of 384 bytes
parameters.notes: Decisions D-09-01, D-09-03 and D-09-04 (phase-09-traceability.md). No earlier document fixed a secret size or count. 16 KiB holds passwords, recovery codes, API tokens and PEM-encoded keys and keeps the request far inside the 128 KiB body limit, which is unchanged. The database refuses a larger payload and a lifetime over 7 days (migration 20261009000000_burn_secrets)
